catalog_quote: [p. 22] 2.7. Unsur Suprasegmental Untuk mengetahui unsur suprasegmental dalam bahasa Siang, maka dapat dilihat hal-hal berikut ini. [p. 23] 1) Kata bersuku satu mendapat tekanan pada suku pertama Contoh : yuh 'ya', tuh 'ini', non 'itu', moh 'mana', kuh 'ku' 2) Kata yang bersuku dua mendapat tekanan pada suku pertama Contoh : bulu 'babi', nawui 'menabur', tandu 'usungan', belei 'burung', cohit 'gembira' 3) Kata yang bersuku tiga mendapat tekanan pada suku terakhir Contoh : pompatoi 'kematian', kalowon 'kuburan', kosusah 'kesusahan', nomulun 'menghidupi', noranka 'merangkak' 4) Kata yang bersuku empat mendapat tekanan pada suku pertama. Contoh : ponkususah 'paling susah', tononkumo 'dirasakan', tonosilit 'dilarang', tolobowoh 'laron', katepkala 'kalajengking' [p. 80] Fonem suprasegmental tidak terdapat dalam bahasa Siang, sebab perbedaan tekanan, nada, dan kuantitas (panjang pendek) tidak membedakan arti suatu kata. Dalam hal tekanan kata dalam bahasa Siang pada umumnya kata bersuku dua mendapat tekanan pada suku kata kedua, kata bersuku tiga mendapat tekanan pada suku kata terakhir, dan kata bersuku empat mendapat tekanan pada suku kata pertama.

new_statements.translation: [p. 23] 1) Monosyllabic words are stressed on the first syllable ... 2) Disyllabic words are stressed on the first syllable. Examples: bulu 'pig', nawui 'sow', tandu 'litter', belei 'bird', cohit 'glad'. 3) Trisyllabic words are stressed on the last syllable. Examples: pompatoi 'death', kalowon 'grave' ... 4) Four-syllable words are stressed on the first syllable. ... [p. 80] There are no suprasegmental phonemes in Siang, because differences of stress, pitch and quantity (length) do not distinguish word meanings. As for word stress in Siang, in general disyllabic words are stressed on the second syllable, trisyllabic words on the last syllable, and four-syllable words on the first syllable.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress is non-contrastive. The authors give a syllable-count-dependent placement: 2-syllable words initial (sec. 2.7) or final (ch. 5 summary -- the two passages contradict each other), 3-syllable words final, 4-syllable words initial. No single edge-based rule is stated and no stress marks are printed on the examples, so the description cannot be reduced to a fixed position.
new_statements.exceptions: None; rules are stated per syllable count with 'pada umumnya' (in general) in the summary.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (kata) stress in citation forms elicited from informants; the same chapter states stress, pitch and length are not phonemic. Variety: Siang of Kecamatan Tanah Siang (Tumbang Nangu, Saripoi, Tumbang Ulu, Mantiat Pari), then Kab. Barito Utara, Kalimantan Tengah.
new_statements.identity_note: Santoso et al. 1990 describe Siang as spoken in Kecamatan Tanah Siang (informants from Tumbang Nangu, Saripoi, Tumbang Ulu, Mantiat Pari; then Kab. Barito Utara, now Kab. Murung Raya, Kalimantan Tengah) = Glottolog sian1254 / ISO sya proper, i.e. Hudson's 'Siang' rather than his 'Murung-2' co-dialect. No separate dialect glottocode involved.

sources.note: Bab II Fonologi sec. 2.7 'Unsur Suprasegmental' (printed pp. 22-23, PDF pp. 37-38): monosyllables and disyllables stressed on the first syllable, trisyllables on the last syllable, four-syllable words on the first syllable (five unmarked examples each). Bab V Kesimpulan (printed p. 80, PDF p. 95): no suprasegmental phonemes (stress, pitch, length not distinctive); disyllables stressed on the SECOND syllable, trisyllables on the last, four-syllable words on the first -- contradicting sec. 2.7 for disyllables.
